purpose: Machine-readable KPI catalog for building a human-labeling dataset and evaluating video-analysis outputs.

source_selection.primary_policy: Use latest kpi scoring.xlsx as the provisional performance/injury schema because it explicitly defines the accuracy-first 720p, camera-routed, multi-delivery model. Do not silently merge the later age workbook because its KPI set and measurement assumptions conflict with the primary model.
precedence: human adjudication guide approved by AMP biomechanics lead

normalization.camera_angle_rule: Determine angle before labeling. Score only KPIs whose allowed angle includes the observed angle; otherwise record null with null_reason=unsupported_camera_angle. Any/profile/computed are not camera views.

anchors.10: The KPI-specific benchmark_10 field in this catalog.
anchors.5: Secondary prompt only: acceptable but with clear room for improvement.
anchors.0_to_3: Secondary prompt only: significant technical flaw requiring attention.
anchors.4_6_7_8_9: No authoritative universal descriptors found; must be defined in the annotation handbook.

performance.anchor_source_note: The primary workbook defines benchmark-as-10 and off-condition prose but not a complete numeric rubric. Generic 10/5/0-3 descriptors come from the secondary age workbook Claude Prompt Template.

aggregation.split_clip: Detect each repeating action burst and cut approximately 2–3 seconds per delivery.
aggregation.kpi_mean: Arithmetic mean of visible per-delivery KPI scores; retain best and worst.
aggregation.missing_kpi: If never visible, primary workbook says redistribute its weight across visible KPIs; secondary prompt says proportionally. Exact denominator and minimum-coverage rule require owner approval.
aggregation.total_rating: Sum weighted contributions, nominally out of 100.
aggregation.consistency: Derived from spread of per-delivery scores; no authoritative dispersion-to-0–10 formula found.
aggregation.fatigue: Compare early vs late deliveries; no authoritative split size or delta threshold found.

injury.aggregate: Worst flag seen across deliveries for each marker: RED > AMBER > GREEN.
injury.rating_effect: Separate screening pass; must not change the performance rating.
injury.action: Any RED, pain, or young-player spine flag routes to physio; screening aid only, not diagnosis.

discipline.spin: Use unified spin set; off/leg type and variation are profile metadata, not inferred from vision.

sex_model.women: Batting base with female backlift benchmark variant + pace_women + unified spin. Primary workbook says spin is intentionally identical due limited female-specific evidence.

age_primary_model.performance_effect: No approved age adjustment in the accuracy-first primary workbook.
age_primary_model.injury_metadata_rule: Young/Growing marker: SAFE adult; MONITOR age 18–21; HIGH age 15–18; if 15–18, escalate every spine flag one band.
age_primary_model.boundary_issue: Age 18 appears in both HIGH 15–18 and MONITOR 18–21; ages below 15 are not defined.

age_gender_phv_overlay.reason: Secondary workbook has a different KPI taxonomy and introduces exact degree/cm measurements that conflict with the primary 720p coarse-read rule.

Usually pre-growth-spurt; check for early maturers (>7cm/yr growth) and drop to Circa if so.
mapping.confidence_or_caveat: Moderate — PHV range for girls is 9-15.

Boys' growth spurt starts later — most U13 boys still pre-PHV, but check for early maturers.
mapping.confidence_or_caveat: Moderate — highest individual variation band for boys.

mapping.rationale: Growth spurt usually complete by 15 for girls.
Peak growth-spurt window for boys — most sensitive band for this gender.
Growth long completed; consolidating technical/physical development.
Growth mostly complete by 16-17 for most boys.
mapping.confidence_or_caveat: Moderate-High — late maturers may still be Circa at 17.

anthropometric_context.rule: Height may shift physical benchmarks. Weight is landing-load/injury context only and must not move technique benchmarks or the 0–100 score.

batting.female_specific_change: Backlift Height benchmark rewards a slight lateral loop toward gully/slips; all weights and routing match men.

kpis.name: Feet Width
kpis.meaning: Distance between the feet vs shoulder width.
kpis.benchmark_10: Feet about shoulder-width to 1.3x shoulder-width apart.
kpis.off_condition: Feet almost together (tips over) or splayed very wide (can't stride).
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Setup still: compare the horizontal gap between the two feet to the shoulder width in the same frame. Bucket: narrow / good / wide. Two big landmarks — rock solid at 720p.
kpis.why_it_matters: A base too narrow or too wide breaks balance before a ball is bowled.

kpis.name: Knee Bend in Stance
kpis.meaning: Are the knees softly bent, or locked / over-crouched.
kpis.benchmark_10: Knees softly flexed, athletic, ready to move.
kpis.off_condition: Legs locked dead straight, or squatting so low they can't move.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Setup still: front-leg angle bucket — stiff-straight / soft-bend (good) / deep crouch. Whole-leg angle, high contrast.
kpis.why_it_matters: Straight legs can't push off; a deep crouch can't stride. Both kill first movement.

kpis.name: Upright Posture
kpis.meaning: Is the spine tall and balanced, not hunched or leaning back.
kpis.benchmark_10: Trunk upright or a slight forward tilt, balanced.
kpis.off_condition: Hunched right over, or leaning back away from the ball.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Setup still: trunk line (hip-to-shoulder) vs vertical. Bucket: upright/slight-forward (good) / hunched / leaning back.
kpis.why_it_matters: Posture sets where the head and weight go. Leaning back sends both the wrong way.

kpis.name: Head Over the Base
kpis.meaning: Is the head stacked over the middle of the feet, not tipping out.
kpis.benchmark_10: Head over the mid-point of the feet, level and centred.
kpis.off_condition: Head leaning past the front foot or dropping to leg side before the ball.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Setup still: head blob vs the mid-point of the two feet. Over that point (good) / clearly outside the base. Head POSITION, never eyes.
kpis.why_it_matters: A head starting outside the base is already falling — the root fault everything follows.

kpis.name: Backlift Height
kpis.meaning: How high the bat is lifted before the downswing.
kpis.benchmark_10: Bat lifts to around waist-to-shoulder height or above at the top.
kpis.off_condition: Almost no backlift (bat stays low) — no swing to hit with.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Top-of-backlift still: bat-tip height vs the body (bat is high contrast). Bucket: low (below waist) / medium / high (at/above shoulder).
kpis.why_it_matters: No backlift means no swing and no power. Height is the most reliable backlift read.

women.benchmark_10: Bat lifts to around waist-to-shoulder height or above at the top. For women, a slight LATERAL loop of the backlift toward gully/slips is a positive, not a fault — female research links this lateral backlift to higher bat speed.
women.why_it_matters: No backlift means no swing and no power. In women, a lateral backlift toward gully is specifically linked to more bat speed.

kpis.name: Set & Still at Release
kpis.meaning: Is the player set and balanced when the bowler releases.
kpis.benchmark_10: Quiet and balanced at release; any trigger move is small and finished.
kpis.off_condition: Still lunging or walking across when the ball is released.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Compare the 2-3 frames around bowler release: is the whole body settled, or still making a LARGE movement? Gross body movement, not small sway.
kpis.why_it_matters: If you're still moving when the ball is released, you're late. Set = ready.

kpis.name: Stride Direction
kpis.meaning: Does the front foot move toward the line of the ball or across the body.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front foot strides toward the ball (roughly toward off stump for a straight ball).
kpis.off_condition: Foot doesn't move, or steps across the body and closes the player off.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Front-on: front-foot position before vs at the shot. Bucket: toward the ball / barely moves / across the body.
kpis.why_it_matters: Where the foot goes decides whether you reach the ball or play around your pad.

kpis.name: Stride Length
kpis.meaning: How far the front foot strides.
kpis.benchmark_10: A clear, controlled stride, roughly knee-to-shin length toward the pitch.
kpis.off_condition: No stride (stuck), or a huge overstretch that locks the body up.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] At-shot still (side): gap between the two feet — none / short / good / overstretched.
kpis.why_it_matters: Too short and you never reach it; too long and you can't adjust or balance.

kpis.name: Front Knee Bend on the Shot
kpis.source_name: Front Knee Bend on the Shot
kpis.meaning: Does the front knee bend to keep the body driving forward.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front knee flexes into a bent, driving position (~145-150 deg) on front-foot shots.
kpis.off_condition: Front leg stays stiff so the body stalls, or the knee collapses right down.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Contact still (side): front-knee angle bucket — stiff-straight / good-bend (good) / collapsed.
kpis.why_it_matters: A driving front knee keeps momentum going into the ball. A stiff leg stops it dead.

kpis.name: Body Moving Forward
kpis.meaning: Is the body travelling toward the ball, not falling back.
kpis.benchmark_10: Hips and chest travel forward toward the ball from setup to contact.
kpis.off_condition: Weight stays back or rocks backward onto a static/retreating base.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: track the torso blob horizontally setup to contact. Clear forward shift (good) / static / moving back.
kpis.why_it_matters: Getting the body forward turns a hard ball into an easy one and adds power.

kpis.name: Straight Bat Path
kpis.meaning: Does the bat come down straight in line, not slicing across the ball.
kpis.benchmark_10: Downswing travels in a straight line down to the ball; full face comes through on line.
kpis.off_condition: Bat swings across the line (in-to-out / out-to-in), face not behind the ball.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Behind the stumps or square side-on: track the bat-tip path through the downswing. Straight down the line (good) / angled across.
kpis.why_it_matters: A straight bat gives the biggest margin for error and the full face. Across = edges.

kpis.name: Contact Out Front / Under Body
kpis.meaning: Is the ball met in a controlled position, not reaching or jammed in.
kpis.benchmark_10: Ball met slightly in front on drives, or under the body on defence — arms controlled.
kpis.off_condition: Ball met way out in front (reaching, arms locked) or jammed right under the body.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Contact still (side): hands/bat relative to the front foot and torso. Nicely in front / under body / reaching. Uses arm & bat position, NOT ball-on-bat.
kpis.why_it_matters: Meeting the ball in the right place is where good head and footwork pay off.

kpis.name: Front Elbow Leading
kpis.meaning: Is the front (top) elbow leading the hands on vertical-bat shots.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front elbow up and leading toward the ball, hands following.
kpis.off_condition: Front elbow low and tucked into the side — an all-hands jab.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Downswing/contact still: front-elbow height vs the shoulder. Elbow up & leading (good) / low & tucked.
kpis.why_it_matters: A leading front elbow keeps the bat straight and the shot controlled.

kpis.name: Head Over the Ball at Contact
kpis.source_name: Head Over the Ball at Contact
kpis.meaning: Is the head leaning into the line at contact, not pulling away.
kpis.benchmark_10: Head forward, over or just inside the front knee, into the ball at contact.
kpis.off_condition: Head pulls back or falls to leg side at contact — the 'head falling over' fault.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Contact still (side): head blob vs the front knee. Over/inside the knee (good) / behind it / fallen to leg side. Head POSITION vs a landmark.
kpis.why_it_matters: The head at contact is the payoff of a still setup. If it falls here, the shot falls.

kpis.name: Follow-Through Completion
kpis.meaning: Does the bat finish the swing high, or get checked at contact.
kpis.benchmark_10: Bat continues up into a full, high finish.
kpis.off_condition: Swing stops dead at contact — a checked, jabby finish.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Post-contact (side): does the bat-tip keep travelling up to a high finish, or stop near contact height?
kpis.why_it_matters: A checked finish means the player didn't commit or lost balance mid-shot.

kpis.name: Balance at the Finish
kpis.meaning: Is the player balanced and tall at the end of the shot.
kpis.benchmark_10: Standing balanced and controlled at the finish — no toppling or extra steps.
kpis.off_condition: Falling to one side, or stepping to catch balance after the shot.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Final still: whole body upright and stable, or leaning/stumbling/stepping? One of the easiest 720p reads.
kpis.why_it_matters: A messy finish proves balance broke somewhere upstream — the summary check.

kpis.name: Same Shape Every Ball
kpis.meaning: Is the technique repeatable across the deliveries in the clip.
kpis.benchmark_10: The scores above stay steady from delivery to delivery.
kpis.off_condition: One clean ball then several loose ones — big swings between deliveries.
kpis.observable_check: [COMPUTED] Not vision: measure how much each KPI score varies across the deliveries in the clip. Low variation = high score.
kpis.why_it_matters: Consistency separates a player who looks good once from one you can trust. Only measurable because the clip has several balls.

kpis.name: Run-Up Speed
kpis.meaning: Does the bowler run in with real, controlled speed.
kpis.benchmark_10: A genuinely quick, smooth run-up (elite men ~5-7 m/s). Fastest bowlers have the quickest run-ups.
kpis.off_condition: Walking or jogging in with little momentum.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: how fast the body crosses the screen over the run-up. Bucket: walk / jog / fast. Gross whole-body speed.
kpis.why_it_matters: Run-up speed is the biggest controllable source of pace — momentum you feed into the ball.

kpis.name: Gathers Into the Crease
kpis.meaning: Is the bowler gathering/accelerating into delivery, not slowing.
kpis.benchmark_10: Strides stay quick or quicken into the crease — no braking.
kpis.off_condition: Visibly slowing down in the last few strides.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: last 2 strides vs mid-run-up strides. Quick/gathering (good) / slowing.
kpis.why_it_matters: Braking before delivery throws away the pace the run-up built.

kpis.name: Bound Into Delivery
kpis.meaning: Is there a clear bound/leap into the delivery stride.
kpis.benchmark_10: A controlled bound with height and forward momentum into the crease.
kpis.off_condition: A flat shuffle into the crease with no bound.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] The frame where both feet are off the ground before the delivery stride. Present (good) / absent.
kpis.why_it_matters: The bound sets up the whole delivery stride and load position.

kpis.name: Side-On at the Load
kpis.meaning: Is the body side-on at back-foot landing, or already opened up.
kpis.benchmark_10: Chest/shoulders turned side-on (or controlled front-on), lined up to deliver.
kpis.off_condition: Body chaotically open or twisted at the load.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Back-foot-landing still: shoulder line vs the pitch direction. Side-on / front-on / twisted. (Also feeds the injury sheet.)
kpis.why_it_matters: The load position sets whether the action is powerful and repeatable, or a mess.

kpis.name: Front Foot Landing Position
kpis.meaning: Where the front foot lands relative to the body line.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front foot lands in line or slightly outside off — not across the body.
kpis.off_condition: Front foot lands well across the body, closing the action off.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Front-on front-foot-contact still: front foot in line with the body or across it? Foot vs body midline.
kpis.why_it_matters: Landing across the body forces the trunk to twist and cuts both pace and safety.

kpis.name: Braced Front Leg
kpis.meaning: Does the front leg stay strong at landing, or does the knee buckle.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front leg lands and braces close to straight (knee stays above ~130 deg / under ~50 deg of bend).
kpis.off_condition: Front knee keeps bending after landing — the body sinks instead of levering over.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Side, at release: front-knee angle — braced/straight (good) / collapsing. Big high-contrast joint. The most reliable pace read.
kpis.why_it_matters: A braced front leg converts run-up speed into ball speed. A collapsing knee leaks it into the ground. Top validated speed driver.

kpis.name: Forward Trunk Drive
kpis.meaning: Does the upper body fold forward powerfully through release.
kpis.benchmark_10: Clear forward bend of the trunk from front-foot contact to release, driving the arm over.
kpis.off_condition: Upper body stays upright/stiff or falls away sideways.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: trunk line at front-foot contact vs release. Clear forward fold (good) / upright / falling away.
kpis.why_it_matters: Trunk drive is one of the four validated pace predictors — the big engine the arm rides on.

kpis.name: Arm Height at Release
kpis.meaning: Is the ball released from a high arm or a low sling.
kpis.benchmark_10: Bowling arm high at release (ideally above ~70-85 deg from horizontal).
kpis.off_condition: Low, slingy arm at release.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Release still (side): bowling-arm angle from horizontal — low sling / medium / high. Long high-contrast segment.
kpis.why_it_matters: A high arm gives bounce and carry. One of the most reliable reads on the sheet.

kpis.name: Delayed Arm
kpis.meaning: Is the arm still back and lagging when the body has turned to the batter.
kpis.benchmark_10: At the frame the hips/chest face the batter, the bowling arm is still well back before whipping over.
kpis.off_condition: Arm already up/over as the hips turn — no lag, no whip.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Side, at the frame where hips face the batter: bowling arm still behind / below shoulder (good) or already vertical? Single-frame position, not motion tracking.
kpis.why_it_matters: The lag-then-whip is where the last yards of pace come from. Arm-back angle is the single best speed predictor.

kpis.name: Non-Bowling Arm Pull
kpis.meaning: Does the front arm pull down hard to drive rotation.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front arm pulls down and into the body sharply, driving the shoulders round.
kpis.off_condition: Front arm drifts or flails with no clear pull-down.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side, load to release: does the front arm come down sharply into the body? Sharp pull (good) / drifting.
kpis.why_it_matters: The front-arm pull can add up to ~13% of ball speed by driving rotation.

kpis.name: Release Consistency
kpis.meaning: Is the ball released from the same point every ball.
kpis.benchmark_10: Release point (hand height) stays about the same across the deliveries.
kpis.off_condition: Release point wanders from ball to ball.
kpis.observable_check: [COMPUTED across deliveries] Compare the hand height at release across the deliveries in the clip. Consistent (good) / variable.
kpis.why_it_matters: A repeatable release is what turns pace into control and wickets.

kpis.name: Follow-Through Direction
kpis.meaning: Does the bowler finish toward the batter or fall away.
kpis.benchmark_10: Body continues toward the batter after release, controlled.
kpis.off_condition: Falls away to the side or off the pitch.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Post-release: body carries on toward the batter or veers sideways? Gross body-direction read.
kpis.why_it_matters: Falling away wastes energy sideways and feeds the injury markers.

kpis.name: Landing Balance
kpis.meaning: Is the finish controlled or a stumble.
kpis.benchmark_10: Controlled, balanced landing after delivery.
kpis.off_condition: Stumbling, over-running, stepping off the pitch.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Final still: whole-body balance — controlled / stumbling.
kpis.why_it_matters: A controlled finish means the energy went down the pitch, and it's safer on the body.

pace_women.key_difference: Trunk Drive Through the Ball scores rotation-through from front or side, not men’s forward trunk flexion; Run-Up Speed and Side-On at the Load receive higher weights.

kpis.name: Run-Up Speed
kpis.meaning: Does the bowler run in with real, controlled speed.
kpis.benchmark_10: A genuinely quick, smooth run-up. In WOMEN this is the single strongest driver of ball speed — run-up speed tracks release speed very closely (r≈0.75), stronger than in men.
kpis.off_condition: Walking or jogging in with little momentum.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: how fast the body crosses the screen over the run-up. Bucket: walk / jog / fast. Gross whole-body speed.
kpis.why_it_matters: For female bowlers, run-up speed is THE number-one controllable source of pace. Weighted highest here for that reason.

kpis.name: Gathers Into the Crease
kpis.meaning: Is the bowler gathering/accelerating into delivery, not slowing.
kpis.benchmark_10: Strides stay quick or quicken into the crease — no braking.
kpis.off_condition: Visibly slowing down in the last few strides.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side: last 2 strides vs mid-run-up strides. Quick/gathering (good) / slowing.
kpis.why_it_matters: Braking before delivery throws away the pace the run-up built.

kpis.name: Bound Into Delivery
kpis.meaning: Is there a clear bound/leap into the delivery stride.
kpis.benchmark_10: A controlled bound with height and forward momentum into the crease.
kpis.off_condition: A flat shuffle into the crease with no bound.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] The frame where both feet are off the ground before the delivery stride. Present (good) / absent.
kpis.why_it_matters: The bound sets up the whole delivery stride and load position.

kpis.name: Side-On at the Load
kpis.meaning: Is the body side-on at back-foot landing, or already opened up.
kpis.benchmark_10: Chest/shoulders clearly side-on at back-foot landing. In WOMEN, being more side-on at back-foot contact is linked to faster bowling (it allows a bigger hip-shoulder separation).
kpis.off_condition: Body chaotically open or twisted at the load.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Back-foot-landing still: shoulder line vs the pitch direction. Side-on / front-on / twisted. (Also feeds the injury sheet.)
kpis.why_it_matters: Female-specific: faster women's pace bowlers are more side-on at the load. Weighted up vs the men's model.

kpis.name: Front Foot Landing Position
kpis.meaning: Where the front foot lands relative to the body line.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front foot lands in line or slightly outside off — not across the body.
kpis.off_condition: Front foot lands well across the body, closing the action off.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Front-on front-foot-contact still: front foot in line with the body or across it? Foot vs body midline.
kpis.why_it_matters: Landing across the body forces the trunk to twist and cuts both pace and safety.

kpis.name: Braced Front Leg
kpis.meaning: Does the front leg stay strong at landing, or does the knee buckle.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front leg lands and braces close to straight (knee stays above ~130 deg / under ~50 deg of bend).
kpis.off_condition: Front knee keeps bending after landing — the body sinks instead of levering over.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Side, at release: front-knee angle — braced/straight (good) / collapsing. Big high-contrast joint. The most reliable pace read.
kpis.why_it_matters: A braced front leg converts run-up speed into ball speed. A collapsing knee leaks it into the ground. Top validated speed driver.

kpis.name: Trunk Drive Through the Ball
kpis.meaning: Does the upper body fold forward powerfully through release.
kpis.benchmark_10: The trunk drives powerfully through release. In WOMEN, pace comes more from the trunk ROTATING through the delivery than from folding forward — reward the chest turning through toward the batter; do NOT penalise a more upright, rotational action.
kpis.off_condition: No drive at all — trunk stiff and static, neither folding nor rotating through.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Front-on where possible: does the chest/trunk rotate through toward the batter from front-foot contact to release? Clear rotation-through (good) / stiff, no turn. KEY female difference: score ROTATION, not forward fold (forward fold does not predict pace in women).
kpis.why_it_matters: The single biggest male-female difference in pace: forward trunk flexion predicts pace in men, but in WOMEN it's trunk rotation. Scored the female way here.

kpis.name: Arm Height at Release
kpis.meaning: Is the ball released from a high arm or a low sling.
kpis.benchmark_10: Bowling arm high at release (ideally above ~70-85 deg from horizontal).
kpis.off_condition: Low, slingy arm at release.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Release still (side): bowling-arm angle from horizontal — low sling / medium / high. Long high-contrast segment.
kpis.why_it_matters: A high arm gives bounce and carry. One of the most reliable reads on the sheet.

kpis.name: Delayed Arm
kpis.meaning: Is the arm still back and lagging when the body has turned to the batter.
kpis.benchmark_10: At the frame the hips/chest face the batter, the bowling arm is still well back before whipping over.
kpis.off_condition: Arm already up/over as the hips turn — no lag, no whip.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Side, at the frame where hips face the batter: bowling arm still behind / below shoulder (good) or already vertical? Single-frame position, not motion tracking.
kpis.why_it_matters: The lag-then-whip is where the last yards of pace come from. Arm-back angle is the single best speed predictor.

kpis.name: Non-Bowling Arm Pull
kpis.meaning: Does the front arm pull down hard to drive rotation.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front arm pulls down and into the body sharply, driving the shoulders round.
kpis.off_condition: Front arm drifts or flails with no clear pull-down.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side, load to release: does the front arm come down sharply into the body? Sharp pull (good) / drifting.
kpis.why_it_matters: The front-arm pull can add up to ~13% of ball speed by driving rotation.

kpis.name: Release Consistency
kpis.meaning: Is the ball released from the same point every ball.
kpis.benchmark_10: Release point (hand height) stays about the same across the deliveries.
kpis.off_condition: Release point wanders from ball to ball.
kpis.observable_check: [COMPUTED across deliveries] Compare the hand height at release across the deliveries in the clip. Consistent (good) / variable.
kpis.why_it_matters: A repeatable release is what turns pace into control and wickets.

kpis.name: Follow-Through Direction
kpis.meaning: Does the bowler finish toward the batter or fall away.
kpis.benchmark_10: Body continues toward the batter after release, controlled.
kpis.off_condition: Falls away to the side or off the pitch.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Post-release: body carries on toward the batter or veers sideways? Gross body-direction read.
kpis.why_it_matters: Falling away wastes energy sideways and feeds the injury markers.

kpis.name: Landing Balance
kpis.meaning: Is the finish controlled or a stumble.
kpis.benchmark_10: Controlled, balanced landing after delivery.
kpis.off_condition: Stumbling, over-running, stepping off the pitch.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Final still: whole-body balance — controlled / stumbling.
kpis.why_it_matters: A controlled finish means the energy went down the pitch, and it's safer on the body.

kpis.name: Side-On Coil at Load
kpis.meaning: Do the shoulders turn side-on and coil before release, using the body.
kpis.benchmark_10: Chest and shoulders turn side-on and coil at the load, winding the body up to unwind through the ball.
kpis.off_condition: Body stays open/front-on — an all-arm push with no coil.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Back-foot-landing/load still: shoulder line vs the pitch direction. Side-on/coiled (good) / open/front-on.
kpis.why_it_matters: Coil is the store of energy the whole delivery unwinds from. Weak, flat spin almost always traces back to no coil.

kpis.name: Front Foot Landing
kpis.meaning: Does the front foot land balanced, not wide or across.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front foot lands stable and roughly straight, letting the body rotate over it.
kpis.off_condition: Front foot lands very wide or across the body.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Front-on front-foot-contact still: foot position vs body midline — balanced / wide / across.
kpis.why_it_matters: A balanced front foot is the platform the pivot turns on.

kpis.name: Front Knee Stability
kpis.meaning: Does the front leg stay stable as a pivot, or collapse.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front leg braces to give a stable pivot for the body to rotate over.
kpis.off_condition: Front knee collapses, killing the pivot and drive.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Contact still (side): front-knee angle — stable/braced (good) / collapsing.
kpis.why_it_matters: A stable front leg turns coil into revs. A collapsing one is the start of falling away.

kpis.name: Body Pivot & Drive Forward
kpis.meaning: Does the body pivot over the front leg and drive toward the batter.
kpis.benchmark_10: Body rotates over a braced front leg and drives forward toward the batter.
kpis.off_condition: Body falls away to the side instead of driving through.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Load to follow-through: torso drives forward toward the batter or veers sideways?
kpis.why_it_matters: The pivot-and-drive turns coil into revs and pace. Falling away is the most common spin fault.

kpis.name: Arm Height at Release
kpis.meaning: Is the arm high at release.
kpis.benchmark_10: Arm high at release. (Off-spinners tend to release from a higher arm than leg-spinners — bowler type comes from the player profile, not vision.)
kpis.off_condition: Low, short-arm push at release.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Release still (side): arm angle — low / medium / high. Long high-contrast segment.
kpis.why_it_matters: A high arm gives flight, bounce and over-spin. The easiest reliable spin read.

kpis.name: Full Shoulder Rotation
kpis.meaning: Do the shoulders rotate all the way through the delivery.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front shoulder finishes pointing at or past the batter — a full turn.
kpis.off_condition: Restricted, short shoulder turn — the ball is pushed, not spun.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Follow-through still: front shoulder pointing at/past the batter (full, good) or still side-on (restricted)? Single-frame position.
kpis.why_it_matters: Full shoulder rotation is what actually spins the ball once the coil is there.

kpis.name: Non-Bowling Arm Pull-Down
kpis.meaning: Does the front arm pull down to drive the rotation.
kpis.benchmark_10: Front arm pulls down sharply into the body, driving the shoulders round.
kpis.off_condition: Front arm drifts with no clear pull.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Load to release: does the front arm come down sharply? Sharp pull (good) / drifting.
kpis.why_it_matters: The front-arm pull-down is what powers the shoulder rotation.

kpis.name: Loop & Flight
kpis.meaning: Does the ball leave with clear over-spin so it loops up above the eyeline.
kpis.benchmark_10: The ball is given air — it loops up above the bowler's release height before pitching, not fired flat.
kpis.off_condition: Flat, darted trajectory with no loop.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Side, plain background: track the ball's path over the post-release frames. Clear upward loop (good) / flat. The one flight cue a phone can read.
kpis.why_it_matters: Loop is the visible proof the ball is spun. (Exact seam, grip and 'dip in degrees' are NOT scored — a phone can't see them.)

kpis.name: Same Action Every Ball
kpis.meaning: Does every ball look the same, so variations are hidden.
kpis.benchmark_10: Run-up, arm and body look identical ball to ball, so variations can't be read.
kpis.off_condition: A visible change in run-up or arm that telegraphs the variation.
kpis.observable_check: [COMPUTED across deliveries] Compare the action across the deliveries in the clip. Identical (good) / visible tell. Judges the ACTION, not the grip. The only variation cue that is 720p-visible.
kpis.why_it_matters: Disguise is what makes spin dangerous. A readable action is easy to line up.

kpis.name: Follow-Through Direction
kpis.meaning: Does the bowler finish toward the batter.
kpis.benchmark_10: Body finishes toward the batter, controlled.
kpis.off_condition: Falls away sideways.
kpis.observable_check: [FRAMES] Post-release: body direction toward batter vs sideways.
kpis.why_it_matters: A controlled finish means the drive went down the pitch.

kpis.name: Balance at Finish
kpis.meaning: Is the finish balanced.
kpis.benchmark_10: Balanced, controlled finish.
kpis.off_condition: Stumbling or falling away at the end.
kpis.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Final still: whole-body balance — controlled / stumbling.
kpis.why_it_matters: A messy finish shows the pivot and drive broke down.

markers.name: Sideways Back Lean
markers.meaning: How far the trunk leans sideways (away from the bowling arm) around release.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE <15 deg · MONITOR 15-25 deg · HIGH >25 deg.
markers.observable_check: [1 FRAME] At release: coarse sideways tilt of the trunk line vs vertical. Bucket into the three bands.
markers.why_it_matters: Strongest predictor of lower-back stress fractures in fast bowlers. Female bowlers carry high lumbar-stress risk too — same marker, watch it for both.

markers.name: Twisting Back (Mixed Action)
markers.meaning: Do the shoulders re-align from side-on back toward front-on after the back foot lands.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE little change · MONITOR some · HIGH clear twist (hip-shoulder gap >40 deg).
markers.observable_check: [FRAMES] Behind the bowler: shoulder line at back-foot contact vs front-foot contact. Little change (safe) / clear re-alignment (risk). NEEDS a behind angle — skip otherwise.
markers.why_it_matters: The mixed action is the best-known cause of career-ending lumbar stress fractures, worst in teens of both sexes.

markers.name: Over-Arching the Back
markers.meaning: Does the lower back arch backward (hyperextend) at front-foot contact.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE neutral/stacked · MONITOR mild arch · HIGH pronounced backward arch.
markers.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Front-foot-contact still (side): trunk stacked upright (safe) or clearly arched back (risk)? NEEDS a clean side angle.
markers.why_it_matters: Arching + twisting + side-lean together fracture the vulnerable part of the lower-spine bone over time.

markers.name: Front Knee Collapse
markers.meaning: Does the front knee buckle at landing instead of bracing.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE braced/near-straight · MONITOR mild bend · HIGH collapsing.
markers.observable_check: [1 FRAME] Front-foot-contact still (side): front-knee angle — braced (safe) / collapsing (risk).
markers.why_it_matters: A collapsing knee dumps 5-8x body-weight of landing shock up into the spine and lower limb.

markers.name: Rigid Landing (No Give)
markers.meaning: Does the front leg slam down rigid, or absorb the landing.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE absorbed give · MONITOR firm · HIGH rigid, jarring.
markers.observable_check: [FRAMES] Around landing (side): does the ankle/knee visibly give and absorb, or land stiff? Absorbed (safe) / rigid (risk).
markers.why_it_matters: A rigid landing sends the full landing shock straight into the spine instead of absorbing it.

markers.name: Falling Away at the Finish
markers.meaning: Does the body fall away to the side after release rather than driving through.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE drives toward batter · MONITOR mild drift · HIGH clear fall-away.
markers.observable_check: [FRAMES] Post-release: body direction toward batter vs sideways.
markers.why_it_matters: Falling away twists and side-loads the back on every ball, and costs pace too.

markers.name: Worse When Tired
markers.meaning: Do the markers above get WORSE across the deliveries (early balls vs late balls).
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE stable · MONITOR mild drift · HIGH clearly worse on later deliveries.
markers.observable_check: [COMPUTED] Compare the flags on the first deliveries vs the last deliveries in the clip. Getting worse late = risk.
markers.why_it_matters: Most injuries happen tired. A riskier action on later balls is a live warning. This is exactly why the clip holds several deliveries.

markers.name: Young / Growing Player
markers.meaning: Context flag from the player's age, not the video.
markers.flag_thresholds_raw: SAFE adult · MONITOR 18-21 · HIGH 15-18 (growing skeleton). If flagged, treat every back marker one band harsher.
markers.observable_check: [METADATA] Not vision — set from the player's age. If 15-18, escalate every spine flag one band.
markers.why_it_matters: Adolescents are the highest-risk group for lumbar stress fractures, both boys and girls.

data_inventory.finding: No CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL, or Parquet label examples were found under the AMP workspace. The workbooks contain definitions and blank score-entry/formula cells, not a labeled ground-truth dataset.

known_ambiguities_and_risks.detail: The file named latest kpi scoring.xlsx is the clearest accuracy-first architecture, but amp_kpi_full_age_sheets_FINAL.xlsx has a later modification timestamp and a different KPI taxonomy. AMP must approve a single versioned ontology before annotation begins.
Primary KPIs specify benchmark_10 and an off-condition but do not define reproducible anchors for every score 0–9. Freehand 0–10 labels will drift between annotators.
The age workbook asks for exact centimetre/degree thresholds, seam/finger/wrist/eyes/contact reads, while the primary workbook explicitly excludes such fake precision at 720p.

Examples: U9/Circa front-knee target notes say approximately 90–108°/120–144° while the same row quantifier says braced 170–180° and collapsing <150°; U9 batting stride says 30–30cm; male U9 arm-height ranges contain reversed intervals 45–42° and 70–51°.
Same Shape Every Ball, Release Consistency, Same Action Every Ball, and Worse When Tired lack minimum delivery counts, normalization, variance/delta formulas, and confidence thresholds.
Proportional weight redistribution can make ratings with very different camera coverage look comparable. A coverage percentage and minimum required angle set should accompany every rating.
Age 18 overlaps HIGH and MONITOR. Ages below 15 are not categorized by the primary age marker. Lateral-back thresholds differ between primary and age workbooks.

No labeled examples, double-annotation records, adjudication outcomes, or held-out validation set were found. The platform can create labels, but cannot claim accuracy until compared against expert ground truth.
Allowed angle names exist, but angle confidence, mixed/oblique views, mirrored footage, handedness normalization, camera height, distance, and occlusion rules are not defined.
Outputs must remain injury-risk screening and referral guidance, never diagnosis, clearance, or guaranteed injury prevention.
